short: VCVTS's unit targets, speech-trained decoder and F0 predictor (M02, M03, M06) came early but are untested by ablation: standard. No WER, unlike its baselines: evaluation (M12) behind.
position: VCVTS [@wang2022vcvts] changes three components: lips predict the codebook indices of a voice-conversion content encoder (M02), that system is trained on speech alone and reused as the synthesizer (M03), and its decoder adds an F0 predictor (M06). Unit targets reach video-to-speech here earlier than in any other ledger study (Appendix), F0 decoding from video follows vid2voc [@michelsanti2020vocoder], decoder transfer follows TaLNet [@zhang2021talnet]; unit targets became common from 2023 and the other two recur ([later]: [@choi2023intelligible; @kefalas2023large; @kim2025faces]). Each is standard: Table 1 compares whole systems, with no ablation (§3). Evaluation (M12) is behind on protocol: intelligibility is claimed without any word error rate, although both baselines [@prajwal2020learning; @oneata2021speaker] and the best comparable earlier study [@mira2021endtoend] score output with ASR. With Griffin-Lim on both sides, the GRID listener-test lead over Lip2Wav lies inside the 95% intervals (Table 1). Speaker control (M07) is the usual reference-audio embedding.
